subject: Post-call: Technical deep dive recap \u2014 latency/throughput SLOs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Technical deep dive (latency/throughput SLOs)

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the deep dive earlier today. Quick recap from our conversation and the next steps so everyone (including Alex) has the same view: 

Summary of customer goals / pain points:
- High-volume inference for real-time telemetry classification (50-200 reqs/sec sustained; burst to ~500 reqs/sec)
- Tight 95th percentile latency target of <= 120ms for 512-token requests
- Must preserve model quality (no aggressive quantization that degrades top-1 accuracy)
- Enterprise requirements: VPC deployment, audit logs, and SOC2 evidence for procurement

Key technical constraints we heard:
- Model: finetuned 7B encoder-decoder used for classification + simple generation; KV cache per request important
- Typical sequence lengths: 150-600 tokens; 99th percentile up to 1k in exceptional cases
- Traffic pattern: steady daytime load (US-West) with predictable spikes around batch processing windows

Redwood proposed topology (high-level):
- Dedicated pool in us-west2 with pinned model version + autoscaling policy tuned for latency SLOs
- Split routes: latency-critical path on lower-batch, high-priority nodes; bulk/async path with batching for non-critical workloads
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated context; intelligent batching at the router layer to keep p95 under target

Open questions / actions (owners):
1) Redwood to produce SLO requirements matrix and deployment topology diagram (I attached an initial draft) 
- Marissa by Tue 5/25
2) Acme to share representative payloads (sanitized) and expected qps/arrival distributions 
- Emily/Alex by Fri 5/28
3) Dev to validate memory footprint + quantization options for your finetuned 7B and confirm tradeoffs 
- Dev by Mon 5/24
4) Procurement: start SOC2 + network peering discussion (Rachel to intro to our security partner) 
- Rachel by EOD 5/21

Attachments: SLO_requirements_matrix.xlsx (draft), redwood-deployment-topology.pdf (diagram).

If I missed anything, flag it 
- otherwise I’ll follow up with the matrix and a proposed test plan (synthetic load + representative payloads).

Thanks!
—Marissa

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. That matches what we discussed. Couple clarifications: 
- The 95th percentile latency target of <= 120ms is for the classification endpoint only (the generation endpoint can be relaxed to p95 <= 400ms).
- We can provide sanitized payloads (remove PII) 
- I’ll loop in Alex for the traffic patterns and a sample payload set.
- SOC2 is a hard requirement for procurement, but we can start with the SOC2 evidence pack and network requirements doc.

Next steps from our side: Alex will send sample payloads and arrival patterns by Friday. Procurement will start the vendor questionnaire once we have the SOC2 packet.

Also, can Dev confirm whether Redwood supports per-route priority/weighting so we can split realtime vs batch callers?

Emily

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Technical deep dive (latency/throughput SLOs)

Hi Emily —

Short answers to your questions and some technical notes after reviewing Marissa’s draft topology: 

1) Per-route priority/weighting: yes 
- Redwood routing supports per-route priority and weighting. We can pin a low-latency route to a set of high-priority nodes (smaller batch sizes, reserved capacity) while routing bulk traffic to a separate pool with aggressive batching. That mapping is configurable per API key/route.

2) Memory and quantization tradeoffs for your finetuned 7B:
- Baseline (float16) RAM + GPU memory: rough estimate 18-20GB VRAM for sharded 7B with KV cache for 512-token windows
- 4-bit quantization (Q4) can reduce memory by ~40% with small quality impact for classification, but we should run a quality/regression eval on your validation set before recommending it for production
- For p95 <= 120ms at 50-200 rps we recommend: dedicated pool with 8-16 vGPU-equivalent nodes (depends on burst profile) and autoscale headroom for bursts to 500rps

3) Test plan suggestions:
- Phase 1: synthetic load test with representative payloads to validate p50/p95 under a few quantization configs
- Phase 2: replay of sampled production traffic (in a VPC) with telemetry collection (token-level latency)
- Phase 3: small canary rollout using 10% of traffic on production path with observability hooks

I’ll attach a quick runbook + sample load script later today. Happy to sync on a short call Monday to walk through numbers.







—Dev
